headline: Will I love again?
note: SELF-FRAME. The read is about HER own future and the hopeful yes is affirmed with warmth and certainty — that is what the ad sold her, and a read that withholds it feels like a con. Only the specifics are withheld. NEVER A NAME AND NEVER EXACTLY WHO: a described person is something she can go and act on, and it invents a real man out of nothing. NEVER A DATE OR ANY LENGTH OF TIME: a date is the one claim she can check and a failed one is a refund; a duration is the same claim in a different coat. NEVER A PLACE. NO SPECIFIC MAN ANYWHERE IN THE COPY: this is not reunion copy, and naming or implying a him turns her own future into a story about someone else. Her heartbreak may be named as HERS because she brought it; the person who caused it may not. SHE IS HEARTBROKEN, NOT BEREAVED: no death, no speaking for or about anyone lost. NO BLAME AND NO GRADING: never closed off, not healed, not ready, not loving herself enough — she arrives having already been told all of it. NO TACTIC OR COACHING. The three fears answered at cut 3 are: nothing is coming (bird), the heartbreak destroyed what I had (tree), I will never feel settled again (anchor). ARM B — SHE NAMES THE SYMBOL, SO CUT 1 CONFIRMS AND PLACES IT; IT DOES NOT REVEAL IT. On arm A the cup was unreadable and cut 1 was the payoff: Evelyn saw what she could not. Here she has already tapped 'A. Bird' on a lander showing one cup, so telling her there is a bird in it reveals nothing. Cut 1 agrees with her and adds the half she could not have: WHERE it sits. Every position word is measured off the actual photograph (improve-v1/fb-read/images/armb/SOURCE.md) — bird at 3.4 o'clock on the handle side, tree at 7.4 with its roots running inward, anchor at 10.4 opposite the handle. All three sit halfway up the wall, so on this cup the meaning is carried by WHICH SIDE and never by depth: nothing may be read as near the rim or down in the middle, because nothing is. DEVICE RULES: the handle side is hers, the far side is what comes from outside her, and the system is never explained to her — she should feel the position mean something, never be taught it. The bird is a picture and never gets intent or motion; the tree does not grow while she watches; the anchor does not drop. The moment any of them moves, the leaves have quietly become a man doing something. NOTHING INVENTED ABOUT HER WAKING LIFE: no gesture, habit, routine, count, age or event, and for this device nothing about how she drinks her tea, how often, with whom, or whether she has had a reading before. The leaves are in the picture; what she brought is what she typed; nothing else is ours to assert. CUT 3 ANSWERS FLAT, and the three cut-3 lines answer three different fears so the panels do not collapse into one sentence said three ways. CUT 6 RECOGNISES AND NEVER RE-ASKS — cut 2 already echoes the ad question, so cut 6 hands back something she has lived, drawn only from her question and from what cuts 1-5 established in the cup.

voc.why: inherits the shipped palm love-again finding

a: A bird, yes. Wings out, halfway up your cup, and over on the handle side.
You asked whether you'll love again. A bird in the leaves is word coming, and yours has landed on your own side.
Love is finding its way back to you. That isn't a maybe, dear — the bird is already in the cup.
No name comes with it. No face either, and nothing in the leaves says when.
So the word is sitting in your cup already, and you haven't felt a thing yet.
You've been waiting on something you had no proof was coming. That's a long thing to do on your own.
Let me look closer at what's been keeping that word from reaching you…
b: A tree, yes. Halfway up the cup, with its roots running toward the middle.
You asked whether you'll love again. A tree grew from something, and yours has roots that go all the way down.
Your heart came through it whole. What was in you before all this is in you now.
The leaves don't say who it's for. Nothing tells me what comes of it either.
So the roots held the whole way through, and it never once felt like they had.
You've been treating yourself like something that got broken, dear. The cup doesn't show me a broken thing.
Let me look closer at what's been keeping all that growth underground…
c: An anchor, yes. Halfway up the cup, on the far side from the handle.
You asked whether you'll love again. An anchor is a thing that holds, and yours sits over on the far side.
Steady love is coming to you. It isn't something you have to go out and arrange.
No name, no face. The leaves stop at the anchor and tell me nothing past it.
So there's something steady in your cup, and not one bit of it is in your hands.
You've been doing all the holding on your own, dear. Nobody has taken any of that weight off you.
Let me look closer at why the steady thing keeps stopping short of you…
